packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-03 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of this fragment. packet.json was not read.

LAYOUT SURVEY
Two faces of one small parchment scrap, each given as a reduced overview with a ruler (image-001.jpg, image-003.jpg) and one small tile of the written part (image-002.jpg, image-004.jpg; these tiles are only about 390-470 pixels wide, so the script is small in them).

Observations:
- The scrap is a horizontal strip about 8 cm wide and about 4.5 cm high by the ruler, upright as photographed. A fold runs along the foot with two slits in it (sewing or tacket holes); a row of prickings or stitch holes runs along the top edge.
- Face 1 (image-001): about 5 cm of blank parchment at the left, crossed by two or three faint vertical lines (ruling or old folds); writing only in the right 2.5 cm, where 11 lines are preserved as line beginnings. The right edge is torn, so every line loses its end.
- Face 2 (image-003): the mirror of this: 10 lines preserved as line ends at the left 2.5 cm, then about 5 cm of blank parchment to the right. The left edge is torn, so every line loses its beginning.
- The first line of each face is cut through at the top; the last line of each face sits on or under the bottom fold.
- No rubric, no coloured initial, no running title, no underlining, no interlinear gloss visible. Small brown-ink gothic hand, heavily abbreviated, with single letters set off by points.
Tentative interpretation (not observation): the two faces are recto and verso of the same piece, each showing the edge of one text column beside a wide blank margin or blank space. Lines contain point-separated sigla and what look like short references (for example "ff ." followed by "de" and a numeral on Face 2), which is the form of a text with citations; whether this is main text or a surrounding commentary cannot be told, because the crop shows only one column edge and no second block. I do not infer work, author, date or place.

Areas selected: all visible lines on both faces. Nothing legible was left unread, but every line is incomplete.

TRANSCRIPTION

FACE 1 - image-002.jpg (line beginnings; right side of each line torn away)
image-002 l.1: tur?/tui? . [top of line cut; rest lost]
image-002 l.2: s(ed)?/h(oc)? dicat?/dicit? h[..]? [torn]
image-002 l.3: q(uonia)m?/q(ua)n(tum)? illis q(ui)b(us)?/q(uam)uis? [torn]
image-002 l.4: q(ua)m?/q(ui)? sunt posso[torn]   [the letters after "sunt" read p-o-ſ-ſ-o; word incomplete]
image-002 l.5: ut no(tatur)? . s?/g? . e . c . r[..]? [torn]   [three or four single letters each followed by a point; the first is a round s or a g; proposed: s(upra) e(odem) c(apitulo)?]
image-002 l.6: em? l(itte)re?/l(ice)t? est idē . a?[torn]   [first two letters are the end of a word begun on the previous line]
image-002 l.7: renouetur p(ro)p?/p(ro)s?[torn]   [first letter r or i]
image-002 l.8: hudem?/h(uius)dem?/laudem? faciūt?/facult[..]? [torn]
image-002 l.9: et nō tr(an)sacto?/tr(an)sactō [torn]
image-002 l.10: multiplic[..]? [lower parts of letters in the fold; rest torn]
image-002 l.11: si? ne? q(ui)dē?/n[..]quid? [..] [written on the fold, partly hidden; torn]

FACE 2 - image-004.jpg (line ends; left side of each line torn away)
image-004 l.1: [torn] et g(e)n(er)a(liter)?/gr(ati)a? d(icitu)r?   [top of line cut; ends in a d with the -3 shaped sign]
image-004 l.2: [torn] [..]is? tr(an)sacto?/exacto? iuo?/uio?   [first word abraded; a second faint line of writing or offset shows just below the left part of this line]
image-004 l.3: [torn] [..]asse[.]t?. ff . de . b[.]? iij . si .   [reads as a reference: ff, then de, a short abbreviated word, a numeral iij, then si]
image-004 l.4: [torn] [..]ic . s?/g? . e . pastoral(is) .   [same pair of pointed single letters as Face 1 l.5; proposed s(upra) e(odem)?]
image-004 l.5: [torn] falsitatē?/castitatē? . g(o) [with superscript o: (er)go] morta
image-004 l.6: [torn] [.]ctus?/[..]cius? s(u)baudi . et
image-004 l.7: [torn] [..]uire?/[..]uue? hic nich(il) iu(r)?/iū
image-004 l.8: [torn] [..]ib(us) t(antu)m q̄ [q(ue)?/q(uam)?] ex lege
image-004 l.9: [torn] [..]i? in fi(ne)? . s(ed) et s(u)bau[di?]   [word runs to the edge of the column; last letters not supplied beyond what is seen: sbau]
image-004 l.10: [torn] [..]tis? [..] . s?/g? . e .   [written on the fold, partly hidden]

LIMITATIONS AND NOTES
- No line is complete on either face: Face 1 keeps roughly the first 8-12 letters of each line, Face 2 roughly the last 10-14. Connected prose therefore cannot be given; what can be checked later are the short strings, of which the clearest are: "renouetur", "et nō tr(an)sacto", "est idē", "sunt posso..." (Face 1); "pastoral(is)", "s(u)baudi . et", "hic nich(il)", "t(antu)m q̄ ex lege", "s(ed) et s(u)bau...", ".ff. de ... iij. si." and "(er)go morta" (Face 2).
- Which face is recto and which is verso, and so the order of the two faces, is not determinable from these images.
- The tiles are low in pixel count for so small a hand; a larger native tile of the written edge of each face would firm up l.3, l.5 and l.8 of Face 1 and l.1-3 of Face 2. Lifting or flattening the bottom fold would expose the last line of each face.
- The wide blank area on each face was checked in the overviews for marginal notes or ruling numbers: none seen, only faint vertical lines and stains.
- Nothing beyond the rules was done for this packet: only PROMPT.md and image-001 to image-004 were opened; no crops, web or search tools were used.
